input: Test the thesis: AI spending supports Micron's HBM revenue growth through 2027

output.thesis: AI spending supports Micron's HBM revenue growth through 2027

evidence_for.claim: On the fiscal Q4 2026 call, Micron said it has agreements for the vast majority of its calendar 2027 HBM bit supply, at significant year-over-year price increases. In Q&A, management said calendar 2027 HBM prices are 'much higher' than 2026 levels and that most of next year's HBM volume is already sold.

HBM revenue grew faster than Micron's total revenue in fiscal Q4 2026, which ended 2026-09-03. Total revenue was $54.23B, up 379% year over year. Management credited HBM shipments ramping across more customers.
Cloud Memory Business Unit revenue (the unit that includes HBM) was $16,283M in fiscal Q4 2026, up 18% sequentially, at an 83% gross margin. Micron guided fiscal Q1 2027 revenue to $61.5B ± $1.5B.

Micron expects industry HBM bit shipments to grow faster than conventional DRAM through calendar 2028. It expects supply-demand to be 'much tighter' in fiscal 2027 and 2028 than in fiscal 2026. More than 75% of 2027 output is committed. Micron has 26 multi-year strategic customer agreements with take-or-pay volume commitments, about $150B of remaining performance obligations with set pricing, and $32B of customer financial commitments, mostly cash deposits.

TrendForce (forecast of 2026-09-29) expects the industry's blended HBM average selling price to rise 121% year over year in 2027. Local media report Samsung's HBM4 asking prices in the mid-to-high $4 per Gb range, versus about $1.50 per Gb for HBM3E. These are asking prices, not confirmed contracts.

AI spending is still rising. Microsoft expects capex to accelerate in the first half of 2027, citing higher component costs. Alphabet held its 2026 capex at $195-205B. Meta raised the bottom of its 2026 range to $135-145B. Hyperscaler capex is expected to top $1T next year, which is an estimate, not company guidance.

In December 2025, Micron forecast the HBM market growing from about $35B in 2025 to about $100B in 2028, a CAGR of roughly 40%. It also said its calendar 2026 production, including HBM4, was sold out, and that the Singapore HBM packaging facility would contribute meaningfully to supply in calendar 2027.

Micron is working with NVIDIA on a custom HBM4E part ('NV-HBM') for next-generation GPUs and NVLink Fusion platforms. Clean-room work at the Singapore HBM packaging facility is ahead of plan, with first output expected in early calendar 2027.

evidence_against.claim: Micron's HBM revenue share fell to 18% in Q2 2026, from 21% in Q1 2026 (also 21% in Q2-Q4 2025). Samsung rose to 33% from 21% over the same quarter. SK hynix was at 50%.

Reports say NVIDIA may move Rubin Ultra from 12-Hi HBM4E to 8-Hi HBM4, which uses fewer DRAM dies per stack, with 8-Hi adoption rising sharply from mid-2027. Rubin GPU memory bandwidth was cut about 13%, from 22 TB/s to 19.2 TB/s. The article does not say Micron is supplying Rubin Ultra or any 8-Hi parts.

Analysts on the fiscal Q4 2026 call asked about reports that a large customer may cut HBM content per chip ('de-speccing'). Management said HBM demand is outpacing industry demand but did not directly answer whether freed wafers would move to DDR. Management also cited the HBM3E-to-HBM4/4E transition and the HBM trade ratio as headwinds to supply growth.

Micron does not disclose an HBM revenue dollar figure. The fiscal Q4 2026 earnings release does not mention HBM. Cloud Memory gross margin was flat at 83% because higher HBM mix offset higher pricing, so HBM still earns less than conventional DRAM, though price increases are narrowing the gap.

Some hyperscalers have hesitated on capex. Microsoft cut its current-year capex forecast to $170B from $175B, and Alphabet held guidance below analyst estimates. CNBC described this as a 'snag', with GPU-provider delays pushing capacity out to 2027.

Micron expects server memory-content growth to moderate from earlier expectations because of tight supply. Its new HBM-relevant DRAM wafer capacity (Idaho ID1) does not start output until mid-calendar 2027, so 2027 bit growth is limited by supply.

counterarguments: Micron could lose share. Samsung gained 12 points of HBM share in one quarter while Micron fell from 21% to 18% (Counterpoint, 2026-09-02). If Samsung keeps gaining with HBM4, and its HBM4 sells at the highest price, Micron's HBM growth could trail the market even though AI spending is rising.

Less memory per GPU could cap bit demand. Moving Rubin Ultra to 8-Hi stacks and cutting bandwidth about 13% (TrendForce, 2026-10-27) means fewer DRAM dies per GPU. HBM bit demand would then depend on GPU unit growth making up for lower content.

Price, not volume, drives the 2027 growth. Supply is constrained (ID1 output only from mid-2027, HBM trade-ratio headwinds), so most 2027 HBM revenue growth comes from contracted price increases. If customers renegotiate or 'significant increases' turn out smaller than the 121% TrendForce industry figure, growth will be smaller.

The thesis can't be measured directly. Micron gives no HBM revenue number (FQ4 2026 press release), so investors depend on qualitative statements and the Cloud Memory unit, which also includes non-HBM products.

AI capex has hiccups, such as Microsoft's cut to $170B for 2026 and deferred 2027 guidance (CNBC, 2026-10-29). A 2018-style pullback in hyperscaler orders would hit pricing frameworks that have not been fixed in contracts.
key_uncertainties: Micron's actual HBM revenue and HBM bit share in 2027. This would be resolved if Micron disclosed HBM revenue, or by Counterpoint/TrendForce share data for Q3 2026 onward.
Micron's position at NVIDIA in HBM4/HBM4E (Rubin, Rubin Ultra, NV-HBM), and whether it qualifies 8-Hi parts. This would be resolved by NVIDIA or Micron statements on qualification and shipments.

The exact 2027 HBM price increases in Micron's contracts compared with the industry's +121% blended ASP forecast. This would be resolved by management's comments on HBM ASP and Cloud Memory unit revenue per quarter.

How binding the agreements are: what share of 2027 HBM is take-or-pay with fixed prices versus pricing frameworks. The SCA disclosures in the 10-K/10-Q and changes in remaining performance obligations (about $150B) would answer this.
Hyperscalers' 2027 capex budgets. Formal guidance is expected on the Q4 2026 calls in January-February 2027.
what_would_change_the_view: Micron's FQ1 2027 results (around December 2026) falling short of the $61.5B ± $1.5B guide, or Cloud Memory unit revenue declining sequentially.
Counterpoint or TrendForce showing Micron's HBM share below about 15% in late 2026 or 2027, or Samsung winning most of NVIDIA's HBM4/4E allocation.
Confirmation that NVIDIA's 8-Hi shift or de-speccing lowers total HBM bit demand in 2027, or that Micron is left out of Rubin Ultra supply.
Hyperscalers guiding 2027 capex flat or down on their January-February 2027 calls, or customers renegotiating or deferring take-or-pay HBM commitments.
Positive: Micron disclosing HBM revenue or run-rate figures, confirmed 2028 HBM agreements, or the Singapore packaging and ID1 capacity coming online early.
output.verdict: Supported for 2027, with caveats. Micron says it has sold the vast majority of its calendar 2027 HBM bits at significantly higher prices, HBM grew faster than its $54B quarterly revenue, and AI capex is still rising into 2027. The main risks are Micron's falling HBM share (21% to 18% as Samsung gained), NVIDIA possibly using less HBM per GPU, and the lack of any disclosed HBM revenue figure. These threaten how much Micron grows more than whether it grows in 2027.
missing_fields: Micron HBM revenue dollar figure for FQ4 2026 or FQ1 2027 (not disclosed in the press release or call coverage I read)
Micron-specific percentage HBM price increase for calendar 2027
Micron's HBM bit share forecast for 2027 (the UBS ~20% figure appeared only in a search snippet; I did not open that page)
Text of the FQ4 2026 prepared remarks PDF (the PDF could not be read)
Hyperscaler 2027 capex guidance in dollars (no company has issued it)
Amazon's Q3 2026 capex figures (not on the CNBC page I opened)
